questions.question_english: If a formal complaint is received regarding the sexual harassment of a minor female student (below 18 years of age) by a male school teacher, under which primary legislation must the police register the First Information Report (FIR)?
options_english: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009
Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
questions.explanation_english:
When a sexual offence is committed against any person below the age of 18 years (defined as a 'child' under Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act), the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 is the specialized, non-negotiable penal legislation governing the offence.
Although the POSH Act, 2013 covers sexual harassment of women at the workplace, in school settings involving minor students, Section 42A of the POCSO Act clearly provides that POCSO has an overriding effect over other laws in case of any inconsistency. Furthermore, sexual harassment of a child is an offence under Section 11/12 of the POCSO Act (and potentially aggravated sexual assault under Section 9/10 if committed by a person in authority such as a teacher). Therefore, the FIR must be registered under the POCSO Act, 2012 along with relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (formerly IPC).
questions.explanation_hindi:
जब 18 वर्ष से कम आयु के किसी भी बालक/बालिका (पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 2(1)(d) के अनुसार 'बालक') के विरुद्ध कोई लैंगिक अपराध घटित होता है, तो 'लैंगिक अपराधों से बालकों का संरक्षण (POCSO) अधिनियम, 2012' एक विशेष दांडिक विधि के रूप में लागू होता है।
यद्यपि POSH अधिनियम 2013 कार्यस्थल पर महिलाओं की सुरक्षा से संबंधित है, परंतु यदि पीड़िता नाबालिग छात्रा है, तो पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 42A के अध्यारोही प्रभाव (overriding effect) के कारण यह मामला सीधे पॉक्सो अधिनियम के दायरे में आता है। शिक्षक द्वारा नाबालिग छात्रा का उत्पीड़न पॉक्सो की धारा 11/12 (यौन उत्पीड़न) तथा धारा 9/10 (प्राधिकारी व्यक्ति द्वारा गंभीर यौन हमला) के अंतर्गत दंडनीय अपराध है। अतः पुलिस द्वारा FIR अनिवार्य रूप से पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 के तहत दर्ज की जाएगी। इसलिए विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) POCSO Act, 2012

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a sexual offence involves a minor student below eighteen years of age, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 applies as a specialized penal statute. In case of conflict, special laws protecting children prevail, and law enforcement must register the FIR under this specific act.

questions.question_english: Under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, which authority is empowered to frame rules for the calculation and disbursement of compensation to child victims?
options_english: The Central Government or State Government
The Supreme Court of India in consultation with High Courts
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
The District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) operating in the region
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 45 of the POCSO Act, 2012, the Central Government is vested with the power to make rules by notification for carrying out the purposes of the Act. Specifically, under Rule 9 of the POCSO Rules, 2020 (framed by the Central Government), detailed guidelines, criteria, and procedures are prescribed for the assessment, recommendation, and disbursement of interim and final compensation to child victims. Furthermore, Section 33(8) provides that the Special Court may direct the payment of compensation to the child from the Victim Compensation Scheme notified by respective State Governments under Section 357A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) or applicable statutory funds. Therefore, the Central and State Governments possess the statutory authority to frame rules and schemes for calculating, awarding, and disbursing compensation to child victims.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 45 के अंतर्गत केंद्र सरकार को अधिनियम के प्रयोजनों को प्रभावी ढंग से लागू करने हेतु नियम बनाने की शक्ति प्राप्त है। केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिसूचित पॉक्सो नियमावली, 2020 के नियम 9 के तहत पीड़ित बालकों को अंतरिम एवं अंतिम मुआवजे के निर्धारण, मूल्यांकन तथा संवितरण के विस्तृत मानदंड और प्रक्रियाएं तय की गई हैं। इसके अतिरिक्त, धारा 33(8) के अनुसार विशेष न्यायालय दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता (CrPC) की धारा 357A के तहत राज्य सरकारों द्वारा अधिसूचित 'पीड़ित प्रतिकर योजना' (Victim Compensation Scheme) अथवा राज्य/केंद्रीय निधियों से मुआवजा देने का निर्देश दे सकता है। अतः पीड़ित बच्चों के मुआवजे के निर्धारण व वितरण हेतु सांविधिक नियम व नीतियां बनाने का अधिकार केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों को प्राप्त है। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The Central or State Government

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 45 empowers the Central Government, and respective State Governments under statutory rules, to frame rules for calculating, awarding, and disbursing monetary compensation to child victims. These regulations govern interim and final relief, establishing standardized procedures for financial assistance across jurisdictions throughout the nation.

questions.question_english: During a trial under the POCSO Act, the accused requests permission to see the child victim in order to apologize. What should the Special Court do?
options_english: Allow the request, as genuine apology is considered a clear sign of remorse
Deny the request, as Section 33(7) strictly prohibits exposing the child to the accused
Allow the request only in the direct presence and supervision of the child's parents
Postpone the trial proceedings until mutual reconciliation is attempted between the parties
questions.explanation_english: Section 33(7) of the POCSO Act, 2012 mandates that the Special Court shall ensure that the child victim is not exposed in any way to the accused at any point during the recording of evidence or trial proceedings, while simultaneously ensuring that the accused can hear the child's testimony and consult with his defense counsel (e.g., through video-linkage, screens, or single-way mirrors). Direct confrontation or contact between the accused and the child is strictly prohibited because it causes severe psychological intimidation, retraumatization, and acute emotional distress. Moreover, child sexual abuse offences under the POCSO Act are grave non-compoundable criminal offences where no private compromise or conciliation is permitted in law. Thus, the Special Court must firmly deny the accused's request.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 33(7) में यह अनिवार्य किया गया है कि विशेष न्यायालय यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि साक्ष्य दर्ज करते समय अथवा अदालती कार्यवाही के दौरान बालक को किसी भी रूप में अभियुक्त के समक्ष प्रत्यक्ष रूप से न लाया जाए (child is not exposed in any way to the accused)। हालांकि, अभियुक्त को वीडियो कॉन्फ्रेंसिंग या एकतरफा पारदर्शी स्क्रीन के जरिए गवाही सुनने और अपने वकील से परामर्श करने का अधिकार रहता है। बच्चे और अभियुक्त का सीधा आमना-सामना बच्चे में अत्यधिक भय, मानसिक आघात और दबाव पैदा करता है। इसके अतिरिक्त, पॉक्सो के तहत अपराध गैर-शमनीय (non-compoundable) हैं, जिनमें व्यक्तिगत सुलह या माफीनामे का कोई कानूनी स्थान नहीं है। अतः विशेष न्यायालय को अभियुक्त के इस अनुरोध को स्पष्ट रूप से खारिज करना होगा (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Deny it, as Section 33(7) prohibits exposing the child to the accused

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 33(7) mandates that the Special Court shall ensure the child is not exposed to the accused at any point during proceedings. The court must deny requests for direct face-to- face contact, as personal confrontation causes severe emotional distress and violates statutory mandatory child-friendly judicial safeguards.

questions.question_hindi: एक विद्यालय प्राचार्य को आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) की अंतिम जांच रिपोर्ट प्राप्त होती है, जिसमें एक PGT द्वारा TGT के विरुद्ध लैंगिक उत्पीड़न का आरोप सिद्ध पाया गया है। CCS (CCA) नियमावली, 1965 को POSH अधिनियम, 2013 के साथ पढ़ने पर, प्राचार्य/अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी को कैसे आगे बढ़ना चाहिए?

questions.question_english: A Principal receives the ICC's final inquiry report concluding that sexual harassment by a PGT against a TGT is substantiated. Under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, read with the POSH Act, 2013, how must the disciplinary process proceed?
options_english: The Principal must conduct a fresh preliminary inquiry to verify the findings of the ICC
The ICC report is deemed an inquiry report under Rule 14 of CCS (CCA) Rules for direct disciplinary action
The Principal must mandate a police investigation before departmental disciplinary action can be taken
The Principal must convene the School Management Committee to vote on imposing a penalty
questions.explanation_english: Under the proviso to Rule 14(2) of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules], where there is a complaint of sexual harassment within the meaning of Rule 3C of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964, the Complaints Committee established for inquiring into such complaints is deemed to be the Inquiring Authority appointed by the Disciplinary Authority. Therefore, the inquiry report submitted by the ICC is legally treated as a formal inquiry report under Rule 14. The Disciplinary Authority does not conduct any fresh preliminary inquiry; it serves a copy of the inquiry report to the charged government servant for representation and proceeds directly under Rule 15 to take a final disciplinary decision.
questions.explanation_hindi: केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियमावली, 1965 [CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965] के नियम 14(2) के परंतुक (proviso) के अनुसार, CCS (आचरण) नियम, 1964 के नियम 3C के अधीन लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकायतों की जांच के लिए गठित शिकायत समिति (ICC) को अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी द्वारा नियुक्त 'जांच प्राधिकारी' (Inquiring Authority) माना जाता है। परिणामस्वरूप, ICC की रिपोर्ट विधिक रूप से नियम 14 के अंतर्गत जांच रिपोर्ट मानी जाती है। अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी/प्राचार्य को अलग से कोई नई प्रारंभिक जांच कराने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती; बल्कि वह आरोपी कर्मचारी को रिपोर्ट की प्रति देकर उसका अभ्यावेदन मांगता है और सीधे नियम 15 के तहत शास्ति लगाने की प्रक्रिया पूरी करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (b) The ICC report is deemed an inquiry report under CCS Rules for direct action

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: under CCS Rules for direct action Under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, read with the POSH Act, the Internal Complaints Committee functions as the inquiring authority for misconduct charges involving sexual harassment. The committee's report is legally treated as an inquiry report, allowing the disciplinary authority to proceed directly to action.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the recording of a child victim's statement under the POCSO Act, 2012:
I. The statement of the child should be recorded through audio-video electronic means, if possible.
II. The police officer must ensure that the child is comfortable and not exposed to trauma or fear during questioning.
III. The statement must strictly be recorded in English only for official court records.
IV. The statement can be recorded at the child's residence or a place of the child's choice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II, and IV only
I, II, and III only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 24 and Section 26 of the POCSO Act, 2012, specific child-friendly procedures are mandated for recording the child victim's statement:
- Statement I is correct: Section 24(4) provides that the police officer shall record the statement of the child by audio-video electronic means, whenever possible.
- Statement II is correct: Section 24(3) stipulates that the investigating police officer must ensure that the child is not exposed in any way to the accused, is not subjected to fear or trauma, and that questioning is conducted in a reassuring, comfortable atmosphere. Section 24(2) also mandates that the officer must not be in police uniform.
- Statement III is incorrect: There is no requirement whatsoever that the statement must be in English. Section 24(5) and Section 26 clearly establish that the statement must be recorded in the language understood and spoken by the child. Where necessary, the assistance of a certified translator, interpreter, special educator, or child psychologist must be arranged.
- Statement IV is correct: Section 24(1) expressly provides that the statement shall be recorded at the child's residence or at a place of the child's choice, preferably by a woman police officer not below the rank of sub-inspector.
Therefore, Statements I, II, and IV are correct, while Statement III is false.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर A (केवल I, II और IV) है।

पॉक्सो (POCSO) अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 24 और 26 में बालक के बयान दर्ज करने हेतु बाल-अनुकूल (Child-friendly) वैधानिक प्रक्रिया निर्धारित की गई है:
- कथन I सही है: धारा 24(4) के अनुसार, यदि संभव हो तो बालक का बयान ऑडियो-वीडियो इलेक्ट्रॉनिक माध्यम से दर्ज किया जाना चाहिए।
- कथन II सही है: धारा 24(3) के अनुसार, पुलिस अधिकारी यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि पूछताछ के दौरान बच्चे को किसी प्रकार का भय या मानसिक आघात (Trauma) न पहुंचे। धारा 24(2) के तहत पुलिस अधिकारी वर्दी में नहीं होगा।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the recovery and payment of compensation under the POSH Act, 2013:
I. The Act provides for deduction of the compensation amount directly from the salary or wages of the respondent.
II. If the employer is unable to make deductions due to the respondent's absence from duty or cessation of employment, the respondent may be directed to pay the amount directly to the aggrieved woman.
III. If the respondent fails to pay the directed sum, the Internal Committee may forward the recovery order to the District Officer to recover it as an arrear of land revenue.
IV. Compensation awarded to the aggrieved woman must always be funded directly by the employer from institutional funds rather than recovered from the respondent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 13(3)(ii) of the POSH Act, 2013, when allegations of sexual harassment are proved, the Internal Committee recommends deduction of the compensation sum from the respondent's salary or wages (Statement I is correct).
The proviso to Section 13(3) explicitly stipulates that:
1. If the employer is unable to make such deductions from the respondent's salary due to absence from duty or cessation of employment, the employer may direct the respondent to pay such sum directly to the aggrieved woman (Statement II is correct).
2. If the respondent fails to pay the sum, the Internal Committee may forward the recovery order to the District Officer, who shall recover the amount as an arrear of land revenue under the relevant Revenue Recovery Act (Statement III is correct).
Statement IV is incorrect because compensation is a personal statutory liability of the perpetrator (respondent) and is never legally mandated to be paid out of the employer's institutional/corporate funds. Thus, Statements I, II, and III are correct.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(o)(i) of the POSH Act, 2013, a 'workplace' includes any department, organization, undertaking, establishment, enterprise, institution, office, branch or unit thereof which is established, owned, controlled or wholly or substantially financed by funds provided directly or indirectly by the appropriate Government or local authority. Government schools, Navodaya Vidyalayas, Kendriya Vidyalayas, and aided institutions all fall squarely under Section 2(o). questions.question_english: Under Section 31 of the POCSO Act, 2012, which procedural code governs the trial proceedings before a designated Special Court, save as otherwise expressly provided in the Act?

Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Indian Evidence Act, 1872 exclusively in all trials
Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 for all procedural aspects
questions.explanation_english: Section 31 of the POCSO Act, 2012 provides that, save as otherwise provided in the Act, the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) (including provisions regarding bail, bonds, and recording of evidence) shall apply to proceedings before a Special Court. For the purposes of these provisions, the Special Court is deemed to be a Court of Session, and the person conducting prosecution before it is deemed to be a Special Public Prosecutor (under Section 32). While the POCSO Act contains special child-friendly overrides—such as in-camera proceedings (Section 37), prohibiting direct, aggressive cross-examination of the child by the accused (Section 33(2)), and completing trials within one year (Section 35)—the foundational procedural framework remains the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 31 स्पष्ट रूप से प्रावधान करती है कि, जब तक कि इस अधिनियम में अन्यथा प्रदान न किया गया हो, विशेष न्यायालय (Special Court) के समक्ष होने वाली कार्यवाहियों (जमानत और बंधपत्रों के प्रावधानों सहित) पर दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता, 1973 (CrPC) के प्रावधान लागू होंगे। इस प्रयोजन के लिए विशेष न्यायालय को सत्र न्यायालय (Court of Session) माना जाता है तथा अभियोजन का संचालन करने वाले अधिवक्ता को धारा 32 के तहत विशेष लोक अभियोजक माना जाता है। यद्यपि पॉक्सो अधिनियम में बाल-हितैषी विशेष प्रक्रियाएं (जैसे बंद कमरे में सुनवाई, बच्चे से आरोपी द्वारा सीधे जिरह पर रोक, और 1 वर्ष में विचारण पूर्ण करना) शामिल हैं, किंतु सामान्य प्रक्रियात्मक आधार दंड प्रक्रिया संहिता, 1973 ही है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Which section of the POCSO Act, 2012 explicitly prohibits the media from disclosing the identity, name, photograph, or identifying particulars of a child victim?

questions.explanation_english: Section 23 of the POCSO Act, 2012 governs the 'Procedure for media' and strictly bars the disclosure of the child's identity. Under Section 23(1), no person shall make any report or present comments on any child from any form of media or studio or photographic facilities without having complete and authentic information, which may lower the child's reputation or infringe upon their privacy. Section 23(2) categorically prohibits disclosing the name, address, photograph, family details, school, neighborhood, or any other particulars that may lead to revealing the identity of the child in any print, electronic, or digital media, unless the Special Court permits such disclosure in writing in the interest of the child. Section 23(4) prescribes criminal penalties for contravention: imprisonment for a term not less than six months which may extend to one year, or fine, or both. For educational institutions and Principals, Section 23 read with institutional child protection protocols mandates that no student identity or incident details be leaked or shared with the press.

A criminal trial requires proof 'beyond reasonable doubt' to penalize an offender with imprisonment, whereas departmental proceedings determine whether an employee is fit to remain in public/school service based on the 'preponderance of probabilities'. Because child safety in schools is of paramount importance, a Principal/Disciplinary Authority cannot and should not wait for protracted criminal investigations or court judgments before initiating administrative actions—such as immediate suspension and regular departmental inquiry. questions.explanation_english:
Section 35 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 sets strict timelines for legal proceedings to avoid revictimization of child victims:
1. Section 35(1) stipulates that the evidence of the child shall be recorded within a period of thirty days from the date of taking cognizance of the offence, and reasons for any delay must be recorded in writing by the Special Court.

Appointment and qualifications of Special Public Prosecutors
Presumption of culpable mental state and commission of offence

questions.explanation_english: Section 30 of the POCSO Act, 2012 deals with the statutory 'Presumption of culpable mental state'. In conventional criminal jurisprudence under the Indian Evidence Act, the prosecution must prove mens rea (guilty mind) beyond reasonable doubt. However, under Section 30 of the POCSO Act, in any prosecution for any offence under this Act requiring a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court 'shall presume' the existence of such mental state. The Explanation to Section 30 clarifies that 'culpable mental state' includes intention, motive, knowledge of a fact, and belief in or reason to believe a fact. The burden then shifts to the accused to prove beyond reasonable doubt that they did not have such mental state with respect to the act charged. Together with Section 29 (Presumption as to certain offences), Section 30 forms a powerful statutory presumption shifting the legal burden of proof to the accused to safeguard children from sexual abuse.

पॉक्सो (POCSO) अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 30 'आपराधिक मनःस्थिति की उपधारणा' (Presumption of culpable mental state) का वैधानिक प्रावधान करती है।

सामान्य आपराधिक विधि में अभियोजन (Prosecution) को यह सिद्ध करना होता है कि अभियुक्त का इरादा आपराधिक (Mens Rea) था। परंतु पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 30 के अंतर्गत, यदि किसी अपराध के लिए अभियुक्त की आपराधिक मनःस्थिति की आवश्यकता है, तो विशेष न्यायालय यह मानकर चलेगा (Shall Presume) कि अभियुक्त की मनःस्थिति आपराधिक थी।

धारा 30 के स्पष्टीकरण के अनुसार, 'आपराधिक मनःस्थिति' में आशय (Intention), हेतु (Motive), किसी तथ्य का ज्ञान (Knowledge), तथा किसी तथ्य पर विश्वास करने का कारण शामिल है। इसके पश्चात अभियुक्त को उचित संदेह से परे यह साबित करना होता है कि उसका ऐसा कोई आपराधिक आशय नहीं था। धारा 29 (अपराध कारित करने की उपधारणा) और धारा 30 बालकों के विरुद्ध होने वाले गंभीर अपराधों में कठोर दण्ड सुनिश्चित करने के लिए यह उलटा भार (Reverse Burden of Proof) स्थापित करती हैं।

Under Section 5(m), committing penetrative sexual assault on a child below 12 years of age is classified as 'aggravated penetrative sexual assault'. Prior to the 2019 amendment, the minimum punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault was 10 years, which was enhanced to 20 years to reinforce protection for children below 12 years.
